title: URL and history state

Beginner-quality contract 1.0.0 applied deterministically from existing source-linked draft facts; publication stage and reviewer state are unchanged.

sources.locator: MDN JavaScript Guide; accessed 2026-07; provisions applicable to URL and history state
sources.claim: URL and URLSearchParams parse and serialize addresses safely relative to an explicit base instead of manual string concatenation.

canonicalExplanation.summary: Don't build addresses by gluing strings. `new URL(path, base)` parses an address relative to an explicit base, and `url.searchParams.set("q", text)` **encodes** values for you: spaces, `&` and `#` included. Before navigating to an address that came from a user or a query string, check `url.origin` and `url.protocol` so a `?next=` value can't send people to another site or run `javascript:`. To make a page's filters **shareable**, write them into the URL with `history.pushState`, and listen for `popstate` so Back and Forward restore them.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
After sign-in, a page reads `?next=` from the address and runs `location.href = next`. Someone shares a link with `next=https://evil.example`, and learners who sign in land on a fake copy of the site. new URL(userPath, location.origin) is checked for allowed origin and protocol before navigation. In this lesson you'll implement shareable filter state and handle back-forward navigation.

```predict
{"question": "`\"/search?q=\" + \"rock & roll\"` gives a query where q is…", "options": ["\"rock & roll\"", "\"rock \" and a stray parameter named \" roll\""], "answer": 1, "why": "The raw & starts a new parameter. `url.searchParams.set(\"q\", \"rock & roll\")` encodes it correctly."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know the **DOM, events and forms** module, the **Promises, async work and HTTP** module, **Event propagation and delegation** (popstate is an event), and **Relative and absolute URLs** (absolute vs relative addresses).

sections.heading: The rule: parse against a base, then check before you trust
Shareable filters and the Back button

includes: Parse and build URLs with URL and URLSearchParams.
Validate redirects and keep filter state in history with pushState and popstate.

outcomes: Implement shareable filter state and handle back-forward navigation.

examples.title: The redirect that went off-site
examples.situation: new URL(userPath, location.origin) is checked for allowed origin and protocol before the sign-in navigation.
walkthrough: **Parse:** `new URL(next, location.origin)` turns both "/lessons/7" and "https://evil.example" into URL objects.
**Check origin and protocol:** the evil URL's origin differs from location.origin, so safeNext returns "/".
**Test:** safeNext("/lessons/7") will return "/lessons/7", and safeNext("javascript:alert(1)") will return "/".
examples.result: Signed-in learners only ever land on pages of this site, and malicious next links go home instead.

examples.title: The filter that Back forgot
examples.situation: A lesson list filters by topic without changing the URL. Learners can't share a filtered link, and Back leaves the site instead of undoing the filter.
walkthrough: The filter state lived only in a variable.
Write it into the URL with searchParams and history.pushState.
Listen for popstate and re-apply the filters read from the URL.
examples.result: Filtered links can be shared, and Back steps through previous filters.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Concatenating '?' and raw user text always produces a valid encoded query.
misconceptions.correction: Raw text can contain &, #, spaces or = that change the URL's meaning. URLSearchParams and url.searchParams.set encode values so they stay a single parameter.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the opening predict, what did the & in "rock & roll" do?

analogy.example: Building a URL by hand is like **writing an address on an envelope in a hurry**: a stray comma can send it to the wrong street. `new URL` is the post office's form with separate boxes for street, town and notes. Checking the origin is **reading the town before you post it**.
limitations: Envelopes don't run code; javascript: URLs can.
History entries are like keeping copies of every envelope you sent.

steps.explanation: The next parameter comes straight from a shared link.
new URL(userPath, location.origin) parses it against an explicit base.
The origin and protocol are checked before navigation, so it goes home.

trace.textAlternative: Validating a redirect target. Step 1, Input: raw next is https://evil.example. The next parameter comes straight from a shared link. Step 2, Parse: url.origin is https://evil.example. new URL(userPath, location.origin) parses it against an explicit base. Step 3, Check: allowed is no; navigate to is /. The origin and protocol are checked before navigation, so it goes home.

faded.prompt: For "The redirect that went off-site", explain how new URL(userPath, location.origin) is checked for allowed origin and protocol before navigation.
expectedEvidence: Names the example "The redirect that went off-site": new URL(userPath, location.origin) parses the next value.
The origin is compared with location.origin.
The protocol must be http or https.
Signed-in learners only land on pages of this site.

nearTransfer.prompt: Write `buildSearchUrl(text, page)` that returns an absolute URL for /search with q and page encoded. Test with "rock & roll" and "C#".
expectedEvidence: # is encoded, not treated as a fragment.

farTransfer.prompt: Add topic and level filters to a lesson list that are stored in the URL, shareable, restored on load, and restored on Back/Forward. Write tests for load, pushState and popstate.
expectedEvidence: Back and Forward restore previous filters.

remediation.explanation: Whenever you see `+` building a URL, switch to `new URL` and `searchParams`. Whenever a URL comes from outside, **check origin and protocol before navigating**.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The filter that Back forgot".

recap.summary: To implement shareable filter state, parse and build addresses with new URL against an explicit base and searchParams for encoding, check origin and protocol before navigating to untrusted URLs, store filters with history.pushState, and handle back-forward navigation with popstate.
retrievalPrompts: Why not concatenate raw text into a query?
What two properties do you check before a redirect?
Which event lets Back restore filters?
